title: selfcheck allow-rules reads every skill under the root's skills/ directory, so a host project's own skill scripts fail it
goal: skill_text_scripts reads only the kb's sprint, item and backlog skills and the worker file, so a host project's own skills/ directory adds no allow-rules failure

run:
import os, sys, tempfile, json
sys.path.insert(0, "_tools")
import bl_selfcheck as sc
root = tempfile.mkdtemp()
os.makedirs(os.path.join(root, "skills", "mine")); os.makedirs(os.path.join(root, ".claude"))
open(os.path.join(root, "skills", "mine", "SKILL.md"), "w").write("Run python3 _tools/myown.py go first.\n")
json.dump({"permissions": {"allow": ["Bash(git status)"]}}, open(os.path.join(root, ".claude", "settings.json"), "w"))
res = sc.check_allow(root, commands=[], tools=())
print(res["state"], res.get("detail"))
sys.exit(1 if "myown" in str(res.get("detail")) else 0)

notes: Found by the SP-s5k72bhd review of BG-cwitx4zn (headless reviewer session 1b63a864, verified by the reviewer with the repro). In the kb's own clone skills/ holds only backlog, item and sprint, so nothing shows there.
